title: Compositional Mirror views over recurrent depth
hypothesis: For sequences of noncommuting depth operations, a shared recurrent block with a compact Mirror coordinate per step recovers held-out ordered compositions at lower serialized bytes than independent step matrices and improves the quality/byte frontier over a simple low-rank gate.
mirror_insertion: A scalar angle m_t selects a Givens-conjugated view R(m_t) W R(-m_t) of one shared recurrent transition.
physical_object: one learned 16x16 recurrent transition matrix shared across steps
mirror_coordinate: a deterministic scalar Givens-angle code selected by each step operation ID, fully charged with metadata
logical_multiplicity: ordered programs formed from two noncommuting operator views

task.teacher: two noncommuting 2D shears embedded in a 16D identity map
task.primary_metric: held-out relative MSE on unseen ordered programs and inputs

controls: static shared recurrent transition with no coordinate
Universal Transformer-style shared transition with learned depth embeddings and shared low-rank FiLM/gate
generic rank-one residual/gate with the same operation address bits
independent per-symbol matrices as upper reference

development.selection_metric: mean length-6 held-out relative MSE subject to payload and MAC gates

storage.authority: actual serialized torch inference payload bytes
paid_objects: all learned transition matrices and gates
depth embeddings and per-symbol address codes
tensor names, shapes, dtypes, and inference configuration

success_gate: On every fresh world, Mirror has length-6 relative MSE <=1.05x independent per-symbol matrices and either >=20% fewer actual payload bytes than the independent reference or >=10% lower MSE than byte-near low-rank gate (within 10% bytes), with <=1.10x active MAC proxy.
failure_gate: Development Mirror misses quality gate, loses the storage gate without quality gain, or is matched/dominated by simple low-rank gate at byte-near cost; if so fresh remains sealed.
boundaries: Synthetic mechanism only; no LM, NLP, or natural-sequence claim.
Operation IDs are supplied equally to all methods; router learning is outside scope.
Possible code combinations do not count as independent capacity.
All fresh data remain sealed unless development gate passes.
